money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Costa Rican Colon (CRC). You can't exchange Australian money in Costa Rica but you can exchange US dollars. Credit cards are widely accepted. Carry cash if you're travelling to rural areas. Most international hotels and tourist facilities accept credit and debit cards. Ask your bank whether your ATM card will work in Costa Rica.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Visit Costa Rica describes a multicultural, multilingual society including Bribrí, Cabécar, Maleku, Teribe, Bruca, Ngäbe, Huetar and Chorotega Indigenous peoples, and encourages community-based rural tourism; use official transport only. Foreigners must carry ID such as a passport (police usually accept a printed copy, but keep the original available). Drug offences carry a minimum 8-year sentence. Generally welcoming of LGBT+ travellers.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: DGAC publishes a list of companies authorised to operate RPAS (certificate, service and models). Commercial services need an operating certificate under RAC 119; private or commercial pilots need a DGAC certificate of suitability. A foreign operator needs authorisation from its home authority and must show the rules are at least equivalent.

register.name: DGAC list of companies authorised for RPAS operations

items.text: DGAC publishes a list of authorised RPAS companies with certificate or authorisation number, service and RPAS models (revision 35, 17 August 2026).

Paid RPAS services can be done only by persons or companies with an operating certificate (RAC 119) after a formal application (Appendix A2). To operate an RPAS for private or commercial purposes a DGAC certificate of suitability is needed: minimum age 18, secondary school title, medical certificate and a training course.

An operator not under DGAC oversight needs authorisation from its home aviation authority and must show DGAC that those requirements are at least equivalent. A specific procedure for foreign operators was not found.
